items.kind: bug (JS emit crash — the checker admits it)
items.status: OPEN — filed 2026-09-29 (Order 44, papers-44's find 1; the integrator files at the report)
items.title: a closure-typed `&mut` parameter CALLED with a bare place — `f(a.s)` where `f: \|&mut str\| void` — is ACCEPTED (a `fun` with the same parameter refuses the call) and the JS output throws `TypeError: Cannot create property`; native prints the right answer
items.discussion: papers-44 (the Store probes); repro `sweeps/order44/papers-44/probes/store/find_bare_place_call.vl`; B439's family (the `&mut` closure-parameter rule)
items.body: The closure-call path must apply the `fun` path's `&mut` argument rule (refuse a bare place, steer to `&mut a.s`), or the JS emitter must pass a view for the place. Rec: refuse, as `fun` does — one rule. Pin both backends. Sizing S; solver.

items.kind: bug (MISCOMPILE on JS; native refuses the emitted Rust)
items.title: a SHARED VIEW passed to a closure parameter reads as the view's internal PLACE PAIR: `f(&a.city)` into `\|c\| out = c` arrives as `[ [ 'Oslo', '1' ], 0 ]` on JS, `out = c` is accepted without `*`, and native refuses the emitted Rust — blocks the Store macro door's cheap read path (store.md)
items.discussion: papers-44; repro `sweeps/order44/papers-44/probes/store/find_view_closure_read.vl`; B444's family (a `&T` view at a value position); store.md (A142 S7) Q1's read path
items.body: Either the closure parameter is typed `&T` and a read needs `*c` (as a `fun` parameter does), or the call copies. Rec: the `fun` rule — a view parameter is a view, and assigning it to a `T` place without `*` is refused; the emitter reads through the view. Pins on both backends. Sizing S–M; solver.

items.kind: bug (UNSOUND on JS — value semantics; native refuses the emitted Rust)
items.title: `*view` of an AGGREGATE does not COPY on JS: `mut c: P = *v; c.x = 99;` writes 99 into the CALLER's value, and a snapshot `Some(*v)` changes with the next in-place write — rule 1 (a binding copies) is broken at a dereference; native refuses the emitted Rust
items.discussion: papers-44; repro `sweeps/order44/papers-44/probes/store/find_deref_copy_aliases.vl`; spec §6.1 rule 1; B400/B418/B457 (the copy-elision family)
items.body: A dereference of a view is a place the binding does not own, so binding it (or wrapping it) copies — the elision pass must not treat `*v` as the binding's own storage. Pin: mutate the copy, read the original; snapshot, write in place, read the snapshot; both backends. Sizing S; solver, FIRST in its batch (unsound).

items.title: the view-escape rule is inconsistent at FIELDS: `struct { f: \|&mut str\| void }` is refused ('a view cannot escape') while the same closure type nested one level down (inside an `Option` or a second struct) is accepted
items.discussion: papers-44; repro `sweeps/order44/papers-44/probes/store/find_view_field.vl`; B439 (the `&mut` closure parameter read as a capture); B364
items.body: B439 says a `&mut` PARAMETER of a closure type is not an escape; the rule should accept the direct field too (rec), or refuse the nested one — either way the same answer at every depth. Sizing S; solver, with B439.

items.title: a DEFAULTED struct type parameter is ACCEPTED at declaration but never APPLIED: with `struct Ordered<K, V, O = Insertion>`, a signature's `Ordered<str, i32>` is a different type from a literal's `Ordered<str, i32, Insertion>`
items.body: Doors: (a) apply the default wherever the argument is omitted (the declared meaning); (b) refuse a default on a struct parameter until (a) is built. Rec (a) if cheap in the nominal-entries path, else (b) now. Sizing S; solver.

items.title: the native `Map`/`Set` never COMPACT removed entries: a map that churned through 200,000 keys and holds ONE walks every tombstone — 0.130–0.162 s for 2,000 walks against ~0.001 s for a fresh map (release builds) — and its memory stays at the high-water mark
items.discussion: papers-44; repros `sweeps/order44/papers-44/probes/maps/churn_native_*.vl` (JS twin `churn.vl`); reactive-maps-sets.md S0; I9 (the types this becomes `HashMap`/`HashSet`)
items.body: Compact when tombstones exceed live entries (the usual half-full rule), preserving insertion order (the contract — reactive-maps-sets.md Q7). Pin: churn then walk, time bounded; iteration order after compaction equals JS's. Sizing S; native, with reactive-maps-sets.md's S0.
